articles.title: Health condition of Sah, rescued from tunnel after 10 days, is normal
articles.summary: Sanjay Sah, who was rescued alive after ten days from the Trishuli Three “A” tunnel, has been medically examined by the Nepal Army and found to be in normal, stable condition. The army confirmed his health status, assuring the public that he is doing well following the rescue operation.

articles.title: Nepal’s flood response must put children at its centre
articles.summary: The article argues that Nepal’s flood response strategies must prioritize children’s needs and rights. Drawing on the author’s experience with past emergencies, including the 2015 earthquake, it highlights how children are disproportionately affected during disasters. The piece calls for child‑focused policies in relief distribution, shelter, education, and health services, urging the government and aid agencies to integrate child protection measures into all stages of flood management.

articles.title: Amid flood crisis, cooking gas price hiked by Rs 105 in Kathmandu
articles.summary: Amid a flood-induced crisis in Kathmandu Valley, cooking gas (LPG) prices have risen by Rs 105.38 per cylinder. Gas bottlers cite higher transportation costs after a landslide at Krishnabhir blocked the Prithvi Highway, disrupting supply routes. The Nepal Oil Corporation (NOC) has set the new LPG cylinder price at Rs 2,060, affecting households across the capital during the ongoing emergency.

articles.title: UPDATE: Two rescued alive from Trishuli-3A tunnel after Bhotekoshi flood
articles.summary: Two individuals trapped in the Trishuli-3A Hydropower Project tunnel in Rasuwa after the Bhotekoshi flood were rescued alive by a joint team of the Nepali Army and the Armed Police Force. The rescue operation, confirmed by an engineer involved in the effort, took place hours after the flood caused the tunnel collapse, highlighting swift emergency response in the region.

articles.title: For every body inside, a family waits outside
articles.summary: The article describes the somber scene outside the mortuary at Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital in Maharajgunj, Nepal, where families gather anxiously awaiting news about unidentified bodies inside. Some relatives stare at photos of missing loved ones, hoping for identification, while others already feel the weight of grief. The piece highlights the emotional toll on families forced to wait outside, often without clear information, and underscores broader challenges in the hospital’s capacity to manage and identify deceased patients.

articles.title: Why DNA testing matters when disaster victims cannot be identified
articles.summary: After the catastrophic floods and landslides in Rasuwa district, Nepal, only about 100 of the 1,290 bodies recovered have been identified. The article stresses the critical role of DNA testing in confirming the identities of victims when visual identification is impossible. It outlines the challenges faced by authorities, the need for forensic labs, and the emotional relief DNA results provide to grieving families. The piece calls for improved infrastructure, faster processing, and coordinated efforts among government agencies to ensure that all victims are properly identified and returned to their relatives.

articles.title: APF’s Timure team lost 13 of its own. It never left the post
articles.summary: On August 26, a sudden surge of the Bhotekoshi River caused a devastating flood in Timure, a settlement on the China‑Nepal border. The flash flood swept away homes, offices and infrastructure within minutes. The Armed Police Force (APF) team stationed there suffered its heaviest loss, with 13 personnel killed while remaining at their post to assist the affected area.

articles.title: Bangladesh provides $1 million in aid to disaster-hit Nepal
articles.summary: Bangladesh has pledged US$1 million in financial assistance to Nepal to aid relief, recovery and humanitarian operations after severe floods and landslides struck northern Nepal last week. The funds were transferred to Nepal’s Prime Minister’s Disaster Relief Fund, as confirmed by the Bangladesh Embassy in Kathmandu. The aid aims to support affected communities and bolster ongoing emergency response efforts.

articles.title: Voices heard from inside Trishuli-3A tunnel, rescue operation intensified
articles.summary: Rescue teams have intensified their search at the Trishuli-3A Hydropower Project in Rasuwa after the Bhotekoshi flood on August 26 trapped workers inside a tunnel. Engineer Shriram Neupane reported that the Nepali Army, leading the operation, received reports of voices from within the tunnel, prompting a focused effort to locate and extract the survivors. The incident highlights ongoing challenges in Nepal’s flood‑prone regions and the urgent need for coordinated emergency response.

articles.title: Chandra Bahadur Thapa, Arika Gurung named Best Male and Female Athletes at NSJF Sports Awards
articles.summary: At the Nepal Sports Journalists Forum (NSJF) Sports Awards held in Kathmandu, boxer Chandra Bahadur Thapa was named Best Male Athlete, while karateka Arika Gurung received the Best Female Athlete award. Gurung made history by winning the female award for the third consecutive year, becoming the first athlete to achieve such a streak. The ceremony highlighted top performances across Nepal's sports, including boxing, karate and volleyball.

articles.title: 217 students, 15 teachers remain unaccounted for after Bhotekoshi floods
articles.summary: Heavy floods caused by the Bhotekoshi River in Rasuwa district have left at least 217 students and 15 teachers unaccounted for, according to preliminary data from Nepal's Department of Education. Nilkantha Dhakal, director of the department, said the missing individuals are linked to schools in Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading districts. Rescue and relief operations are ongoing, but the full extent of the damage and the whereabouts of the missing remain unclear.

articles.title: Govt announces recovery package for businesses hit by Bhotekoshi floods
articles.summary: The Nepalese government has unveiled a recovery package aimed at businesses impacted by the recent Bhotekoshi floods. Approved in a cabinet meeting on September 3, the plan—proposed by the Ministry of Finance—includes customs duty waivers, tax relief and other concessions to help affected enterprises resume operations. The measures target firms whose commercial vehicles or assets were damaged by the flooding, seeking to mitigate economic losses and support regional recovery.

articles.title: Flood kills up to 15,000 pigs, 150,000 chickens and 500 buffaloes in Nuwakot
articles.summary: Heavy flooding in the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli rivers swept through Nuwakot district, killing an estimated 10,000‑15,000 pigs, about 150,000 commercial chickens and roughly 500 buffaloes, according to a preliminary assessment by the Nepal Veterinary Association. The disaster has caused extensive damage to Nepal’s livestock and poultry sector.

articles.title: Rescue teams enter Upper Trishuli 3A tunnel as search continues
articles.summary: Rescue teams, including personnel from the Nepali Army, have entered the tunnel of the Upper Trishuli-3A Hydropower Project in Kathmandu after clearing soil and rocks caused by severe flooding. The Ministry of Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation confirmed that search and rescue operations are ongoing at the powerhouse site to locate any missing workers and assess damage.

articles.title: Citizen Investment Trust allowed to deposit funds in infrastructure banks
articles.summary: The Nepalese Ministry of Finance has proposed an amendment to the Citizen Investment Trust Act 1991 that would permit the Citizen Investment Trust (CIT) to place its funds in infrastructure development banks and to invest in private equity and venture capital funds. The change aims to broaden CIT's investment scope, supporting the country's infrastructure projects and fostering growth in the private equity and venture capital sectors.

articles.title: A disastrous state of affairs in Nepal
articles.summary: On the first anniversary of the GenZ movement, Nepal is confronting a severe flood crisis that has devastated large parts of the country. The disaster coincides with the arrival of a newly formed government, which now faces the urgent task of coordinating relief efforts, managing displaced populations, and addressing infrastructure damage. Officials are under pressure to demonstrate effective governance amidst criticism over preparedness and response capabilities. The article highlights the scale of the flooding, its impact on communities, and the political challenges the new administration must navigate to restore stability and public confidence.

articles.title: Indian ambassador visits flood-hit hydropower project in Rasuwa
articles.summary: Indian Ambassador to Nepal Naveen Srivastava visited the flood‑hit Syabrubesi area near Chilime in Rasuwa district on September 3 to inspect ongoing tunnel excavation and search operations at a hydropower project buried by the recent Bhotekoshi flood. He met with an Indian technical team deployed to the site, highlighting bilateral cooperation in disaster response and infrastructure recovery.

articles.title: Rasuwa flood lessons: Build fewer, taller and longer bridges
articles.summary: The August 26 flood in the Bhotekoshi River, entering Nepal at Rasuwagadhi, destroyed 41 motorable bridges, washing away 35 and severing the road linking Betrawati, Mailung, Syafrubesi and Rasuwagadhi in Rasuwa. The article examines the disaster’s impact and argues for a revised bridge‑building strategy: constructing fewer bridges that are taller and longer to better withstand future floods, thereby improving resilience of critical transport routes in the region.

articles.title: 46 injured in Rasuwa flood receiving treatment at Kathmandu hospitals
articles.summary: Forty-six flood victims from the recent Rasuwa flash flood and landslides are being treated in Kathmandu's major hospitals. At Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital, 30 of the 77 admitted patients remain under care, while 42 have been discharged and one patient has died. The injured were transported to the capital after the disaster, and local health facilities are managing their treatment.

articles.title: Govt declares public holiday on Gen Z Martyrs’ Day
articles.summary: The Nepalese government announced a nationwide public holiday on September 8 (Bhadra 23, 2083) to honor the martyrs of the Gen Z movement. The decision was approved during a Cabinet meeting at the Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers, with government spokesperson Sasmita Pokhrel conveying the announcement. The holiday aims to recognize the contributions of Gen Z activists who sacrificed their lives for social and political change.

articles.title: Government to provide risk allowance, Rs 1 million relief to rescue personnel
articles.summary: The Nepalese government announced that it will provide risk allowances and meal expenses to security personnel and government employees involved in search and rescue operations after the flooding of the Bhotekoshi River in Rasuwa. The decision, confirmed by Education Minister and government spokesperson Sasmit Pokharel, was made during a Cabinet meeting on Thursday. Additionally, each rescue worker will receive a relief payment of Rs 1 million to support them during the emergency response.

articles.title: What is lost and damaged in Nepal
articles.summary: The article discusses the escalating climate‑related losses and damages Nepal is facing, highlighting the need for a domestic reckoning that matches the country's strong advocacy for global climate justice. It points out that while the Nepali government has taken a firm stance internationally, similar urgency and accountability are required at home to address the impacts on agriculture, water resources, and vulnerable communities. The piece calls for concrete policies, financial mechanisms, and community‑level actions to mitigate and adapt to the worsening climate threats within Nepal.

articles.title: The documentary Devi shown to MPs
articles.summary: The documentary "Devi", which chronicles sexual violence endured by victims during Nepal’s decade‑long Maoist conflict, was screened for members of Parliament. The film highlights the continued suffering of survivors and criticises the government's apathetic response to their demands for justice and reparations. By bringing the issue to lawmakers, the documentary seeks to pressure the state into acknowledging the atrocities and implementing concrete measures to support the victims, who feel abandoned by the political establishment.

articles.title: Temporary burial for flood victims in Nepal
articles.summary: The death toll from the Nepal‑China floods rose to 1,050 a week after the disaster, with about 4,000 people still missing. Temporary burial sites have been set up for victims as authorities grapple with the massive humanitarian crisis. The floods, triggered by heavy monsoon rains, have devastated large areas in both Nepal and bordering regions of China, destroying homes, infrastructure, and farmland. Rescue and relief efforts are ongoing, with the Nepalese government and international agencies coordinating aid, medical assistance, and search operations. The scale of the tragedy has prompted calls for increased disaster preparedness and support for affected communities.

articles.title: Headlines on a climate deadline
articles.summary: Recent international coverage of the devastating floods in Nepal has been criticized for failing to connect the disaster to the broader climate crisis. Analysts argue that media outlets are missing an opportunity to highlight how rising temperatures and erratic weather patterns exacerbate flood risks in the Himalayas. The oversight underscores a larger issue of inadequate climate reporting, which can hinder public awareness and policy action on climate adaptation and mitigation in vulnerable regions like Nepal.
